jobs.title: Steuerfachangestellte (m/w/d) Finanzbuchhaltung
jobs.description: Ihre Zahlen sichern die Versorgung. PraxisEins ist ein familiär geführter, staatlich unterstützter Gesundheitsversorger. Wir sichern die Primärversorgung in der Fläche, mit Hausarzt- und Diabeteszentren und der Migräne- und Kopfschmerzklinik Königstein. Für die PraxisEins-Versorgungssicherungsgesellschaft suchen wir ab Frühjahr oder Sommer 2027 eine Steuerfachangestellte (m/w/d). Sie verantworten unsere Buchhaltung eigenständig und begleiten die Jahresabschlüsse mit unserer Steuerkanzlei. Auf einen Blick Eintritt: Frühjahr oder Sommer 2027 Umfang: Vollzeit oder Teilzeit (ab ca. 30 Std./Woche) Arbeitsort: Frankfurt am Main oder Königstein im Taunus, hybrid Gehalt: 52.000–62.000 € brutto/Jahr (Vollzeit), Teilzeit anteilig Ihre Aufgaben Sie führen die Finanzbuchhaltung eigenständig: Kreditoren, Debitoren, Bank und Anlagenbuchhaltung. Sie erstellen Umsatzsteuer-Voranmeldungen und Monatsabschlüsse. Sie bereiten die Jahresabschlüsse vor und begleiten sie gemeinsam mit unserer Steuerkanzlei. Sie stimmen Konten ab, pflegen Verrechnungen innerhalb der Gruppe und liefern Zahlen für unser Reporting. Sie entwickeln Abläufe weiter, etwa digitale Belegprozesse und Automatisierung. Ein Plus: Sie übernehmen die Lohn- und Gehaltsabrechnung oder wachsen in diese Aufgabe hinein. Ihr Profil Abgeschlossene Ausbildung als Steuerfachangestellte (m/w/d); eine Weiterbildung zur Bilanzbuchhalterin oder Steuerfachwirtin ist willkommen. Mehrere Jahre Erfahrung in der Finanzbuchhaltung und in der Vorbereitung von Jahresabschlüssen, in einer Kanzlei oder einem Unternehmen. Sicherer Umgang mit DATEV und Excel. Erfahrung in der Lohnabrechnung ist ein Plus, aber keine Voraussetzung. Sie arbeiten selbstständig und genau und behalten auch bei mehreren Gesellschaften den Überblick. Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse. Was wir bieten 52.000–62.000 € brutto im Jahr (Vollzeit), Teilzeit anteilig. Hybrides Arbeiten: Präsenz in Frankfurt oder Königstein, der Rest mobil. Flexible Arbeitszeiten, Voll- oder Teilzeit. Eine eigene Buchhaltung statt Mandantenwechsel und Fristendruck einer Kanzlei. Kurze Wege zur Geschäftsführung und ein Team, das Medizin und Wirtschaft zusammenbringt. Bezahlte Weiterbildung, zum Beispiel in Bilanzbuchhaltung oder Lohnabrechnung. 30 Tage Urlaub und ein unbefristeter Vertrag. Klingt nach Ihnen? Bewerben Sie sich direkt hier mit Ihrem Lebenslauf. Ein Anschreiben ist nicht nötig, ein paar Sätze zu Ihrer Motivation freuen uns. Bitte nennen Sie Ihren frühestmöglichen Eintritt und Ihren gewünschten Stundenumfang. Ihr Ansprechpartner ist Vincent Sternberg, Geschäftsführer PraxisEins. Wir freuen uns über Bewerbungen aller Menschen, unabhängig von Geschlecht, Herkunft, Religion, Behinderung, Alter oder sexueller Identität. Schwerbehinderte Bewerberinnen und Bewerber werden bei gleicher Eignung bevorzugt berücksichtigt. Über PraxisEins PraxisEins ist ein staatlich unterstützter Gesundheitsversorger mit einem Fokus auf den Bereichen der hausärztlichen Versorgung, Diabetologie und Schmerztherapie. Unsere Mission Versorgung sichern - Qualitätsmedizin gewährleisten. Als PraxisEins wollen wir die Primärversorgung zukunftsfähig machen – mit digitaler Unterstützung, klaren Prozessen und einem Umfeld, in dem Ärztinnen und Ärzte Medizin wieder mit Freude ausüben können! PraxisEins ist ein Arbeitgeber, der Chancengleichheit fördert und Vielfalt schätzt. Wir freuen uns über alle Bewerbungen und bearbeiten diese völlig unabhängig von Geschlecht, Religionszugehörigkeit, Hautfarbe, Herkunft, sexueller Orientierung, Alter, Familienstand oder Behindertenstatus. Zur besseren Lesbarkeit wird in dieser Stellenanzeige das generische Maskulinum verwendet. Compensation: €52K – €62K • €52K – €62K Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

jobs.title: M&A Intern (m/w/d)
jobs.description: Unsere erfahrenen Kollegen kommen von führenden Unternehmen wie BCG, McKinsey, Goldman Sachs und Oaktree Capital und haben bereits erfolgreich HealthTech-Rollups auf- und ausgebaut. Wenn du eine Karriere im M&A, Private Equity oder Investmentbanking anstrebst und hands-on Erfahrung in einem dynamischen Umfeld sammeln willst, bist du bei uns richtig! Deine Aufgaben M&A-Prozesse : Unterstützung in der Strategie und Umsetzung von Praxisakquisitionen, einschließlich Due Diligence und Finanzmodellierung. Markt- und Finanzdatenanalyse : Verantwortung für die Aufbereitung und Analyse von Finanz- und Marktdaten, die für Investmententscheidungen relevant sind. Sparring mit dem Leadership-Team : Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit unseren Führungskräften bei wichtigen M&A-Themen und strategischen Entscheidungen. We believe that automating the ordinary frees humans to do the extraordinary, and we're building the end-to-end robotics infrastructure to make that possible - hardware, software, and AI in one stack that just works. As our (Senior) Electrical Systems Engineer (m/f/d), you own the electrical backbone of our robots, from industrial manipulators to our bimanual platform Alfie. In this key role, you are responsible for the complete electrical system of a robot, not one section of it. You define the power, grounding and shielding concepts, engineer the wire harnesses through moving joints, and take them from first prototype to series supply. If you come from automotive Bordnetz development, you will find familiar work at a very different pace: concepts turn into running prototypes within weeks, and your decisions go straight into products at our customers. Your Responsibilities Own the electrical system architecture of our robots: power distribution concept, load distribution, fusing (Absicherung), wire cross-section sizing and data signal integrity. Define grounding/earthing and shielding concepts (Versorgungs- und Massekonzepte) and design for EMC from the first concept onwards. Plan and support EMC pre-compliance and certification testing, analyse findings and implement robust fixes. Specify wire harnesses, connectors, contacts and cables, and create wiring diagrams (Kabelschaltpläne), harness drawings and BOMs that suppliers can produce from directly. Route harnesses through rotating joints and moving axes: select flex- and torsion-rated cables and drive cable life tests together with mechanical engineering. Work closely with our electronics team on interfaces, connectors, power distribution boards and safety circuits. Use your expertise to inform and provide feedback on assembly procedures, build initial samples and support production engineers with new assembly procedures. Work hand in hand with our prototyping technicians, who build your designs, and turn their feedback into better harnesses. jobs.title: Founding GTM Associate
jobs.description: About Andercore Andercore is the AI-native supplier of industrial materials and goods for energy and infrastructure. We execute trade and distribution end-to-end, on our own account, at the speed of compute - and we are becoming the supplier of record for the entire industry. Industrial procurement is a €900B market in Europe alone and the largest manual market on earth. 95% of customers have no direct access to global supply chains. Materials pass through four or five intermediaries before they reach a site, and 40% of the margin evaporates on the way. For decades, the operating system of this industry was people: people to source, negotiate, finance, ship, and sell. We built the alternative from scratch. We are the supplier. We buy from global sources and sell to European customers on our own account. Our AI runs the full trade: sourcing, quality, pricing, sales, logistics, credit, and financing. One request. A firm quote in minutes. Delivered on time. For the customer, it feels like buying from their preferred local supplier. No warehouses. No fleet. No inventory risk. Every trade is pre-sold before it is bought. We are also the credit counterparty. Customers are scored and insured in minutes and get up to 60 days of payment terms priced into the quote itself. The working capital behind every trade is bank-funded, not equity-funded. Where we are today: Strong triple-digit-million euro turnover run rate, the majority of it from repeat customers Seven European markets live, sourced from suppliers across Asia and beyond 80+ people across Berlin (HQ), London, and Shanghai $90M raised in equity and debt, including our $40M Series B, from Atomico, Project A, Target Global, and Inven Capital - with working capital facilities from UniCredit and KfW The margin is in the bits. The moat is in the atoms. We are building the supplier of record for industrial materials - and redefining how global trade works in one of the largest and most essential industries on earth. The role You build a new business line at Andercore from zero. You win the first customers yourself, you build the sales and service system behind them, and you own the number. No playbook, no handover. The CEO is your direct counterpart. We have built this before in one category. You do it again for the next one. What you own First customers: you find them, call them, close them. Your own pipeline from day one. Sales system: segmentation, pricing logic, offer process, CRM discipline, reporting. Built by you, documented, then handed to a team. Service system: onboarding, delivery follow-up, claims, repeat orders. The customer experience is yours until it runs without you. Supplier side: you work with Procurement on sourcing and price for your category. Team: your first hires, once the system works. Targets First 90 days: the first customers won. First 12 months: a category that stands on its own, with a documented sales and service system. Who you are You were among the best in your peer group: top university, top sales rank, a founder, or a fast promotion. We want to see the proof. At least 2 years of experience in sales, business building, consulting, banking, VC or as a founder. You have closed deals yourself and can name the number: your biggest deal, your quota, your hit rate. You talk to strangers easily. Phone, LinkedIn, trade show, door. You are fast. You decide with 70 percent of the information and fix it on the way. You want ownership and the upside that comes with it, not a title. Fluent English. German is a plus. Our hiring process We keep things focused, transparent and efficient. Meet the CEO (30 minutes) – A chance to get to know each other, discuss your track record, dive into your numbers and hear about the deal you're most proud of. Further conversations – Two to three interviews with key members of the team to explore your experience, approach and potential fit. Meet us in Berlin – An on-site visit to experience our team, culture and working environment

jobs.title: Account Executive (m/w/d) – Berlin
jobs.description: Die Rechtsbranche wird gerade durch KI neu gebaut. JUPUS baut die erste KI, die bis zu 80 % der Arbeit in Anwaltskanzleien selbstständig erledigt. In nur drei Jahren ist JUPUS mit über 80 Mitarbeitenden in Köln und Berlin sowie einem international aufgestellten Tech- und Product-Team zu einem der am schnellsten wachsenden Legal-Tech-Unternehmen Europas geworden. Über 2.000 Anwältinnen und Anwälte arbeiten bereits mit JUPUS. Und wir stehen erst am Anfang. Deshalb suchen wir Account Executives, die nicht einfach nur Software verkaufen wollen, sondern Lust haben, einen neuen Markt mit aufzubauen, Verantwortung für ihren eigenen Erfolg zu übernehmen und gemeinsam mit uns eine ganze Branche zu verändern. Was dich bei JUPUS erwartet: Ein Produkt mit echtem Pain: Du verkaufst keine Nice-to-have-Software, sondern eine Lösung für konkrete Herausforderungen im Arbeitsalltag von Kanzleien. Full-Cycle Sales mit Ownership: Du verantwortest deine Pipeline und deine Deals – von der ersten Opportunity bis zum Closing. AI + perfektes Markt-Timing: Du arbeitest in einem Markt, der gerade fundamental durch neue Technologie verändert wird. High Velocity: Viele Gespräche, schnelle Sales Cycles, klare Targets und die Möglichkeit, unmittelbar Einfluss auf deinen Erfolg zu nehmen. Kurze Wege: Du arbeitest eng mit Sales Leadership, Foundern sowie Product & Tech zusammen. Hohe Standards ohne Ellenbogenkultur: Wir wollen gewinnen – als Team. Schnelle Entwicklung: Wer performt und Verantwortung übernimmt, bekommt bei JUPUS die Möglichkeit, schnell den nächsten Schritt zu gehen. Was du bei uns machst: Du baust aktiv deine eigene Pipeline auf – über Outbound, Inbound und neue Wege, die du selbst mitentwickelst. Du führst Discovery- und Demo-Gespräche mit Kanzleien und verstehst schnell, wo ihre größten Herausforderungen liegen. Du übersetzt diese Herausforderungen in einen klaren Business Case für JUPUS. Du steuerst deine Opportunities eigenverantwortlich durch den gesamten Sales Cycle bis zum Closing. Du beherrschst Einwandbehandlung, Follow-ups und Verhandlung und weißt, wie aus Interesse ein Abschluss wird. Du arbeitest eng mit SDRs, Marketing und Revenue Operations zusammen. Du bringst deine Erfahrungen und Ideen ein und entwickelst gemeinsam mit uns Talk Tracks, Prozesse und unser Sales Playbook weiter. Wer bei JUPUS erfolgreich wird: Du musst nicht aus der Rechtsbranche kommen. Viel wichtiger ist uns, wie du Vertrieb verstehst. Bei der LOHFERT & LOHFERT AG setzen wir uns für ein modernes und nachhaltiges Klinikmanagement ein – effizient, qualitätssichernd und patientenorientiert. Seit mehr als 50 Jahren sind wir eine der führenden Beratungsgesellschaften für Krankenhäuser in Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz und stehen mit über 4.000 erfolgreich abgeschlossenen Projekten für ein wirtschaftliches und qualitätsgesichertes Klinikmanagement. Wir beraten Krankenhäuser ganzheitlich – von der wirtschaftlichen Planung, über die medizinische Strategie und Betriebsorganisation bis hin zur Digitalisierung. Auch bei Bau- und Masterplanungen stehen wir unseren Kund:innen zur Seite, indem wir zukunftsfähige Betriebsorganisationsplanungen und leistungsadaptierte Raum- und Funktionsprogramme erstellen. Wir entwickeln eigene digitale Tools, die wir sowohl bei unseren Kund:innen als auch intern einsetzen. jobs.description: Help Us Change the Way the World Works Build something that matters. Langdock exists to change the way the world works, bridging the gap between what technology can do and what people actually do with it. We bring all leading AI models into one secure, model-agnostic platform and make them usable across entire organizations. Over 10,000 companies use our platform every day, from fast-growing startups to some of Europe's largest enterprises. Their employees open Langdock to draft strategies, analyze documents, or automate workflows - helping them to work smarter, think more creatively, and reach their full potential. About the Role This is a full-time, 12-month program at our Berlin HQ for people who want to understand AI rather than just use it. It begins where our product meets the real world: customer support. Many support tickets are a small puzzle about how large language models and cloud software behave in production. Why did the same prompt give two different answers? Why did a long document get cut off? Why is one model fast today and slow tomorrow? Why did an agent call the wrong tool? Why did an API integration time out? You will be the person who works out what is actually going on and explains it clearly. For most of your first year, the support queue is your home base and your classroom. Few jobs expose you to as many real AI systems, real enterprise environments, and real failure modes, every single day. The purpose of the year: by month twelve, you should understand our platform and operations deeply, from the chat interface down to the models and infrastructure behind it. A Langdock business team should want to hire you permanently, and you should have found the work that energizes you most. What You Will Learn to Understand Customers ask the questions that the rest of the world is still figuring out. To answer them, you will build real intuition for: How LLMs actually behave : tokens and context windows, sampling and non-determinism, hallucinations, prompt sensitivity, system prompts, and why models from different providers react differently to the same input. Agents, tools, and retrieval : how agents plan and call tools, how knowledge bases and document search feed context to a model, and where these chains tend to break. Cloud software in production : APIs, authentication and SSO, rate limits, latency, integrations, multi-tenant enterprise setups, data residency, and access control. Inference and compute : what happens when a request hits a model, why throughput, latency, and cost trade off against each other, and how running our own inference changes what we can offer customers. Daily operational tasks : resolving billing issues, reporting bugs and being the point of for our customers. You do not need to know all of this on day one. You need to be the kind of person who cannot stop asking why until you do. How the Year Works Onboarding: Learn the platform by supporting it. You go through an intensive onboarding into our products, the underlying models, and the support queue. You shadow your first tickets, get to know our systems, and start resolving real customer issues. Expect plenty of experimenting, plenty of questions, and a steep learning curve. Post-Onboarding: Own the queue and take on sidequests. Alongside the queue, you start picking up work from other teams: tasks below the threshold for a specialist to own but too valuable for your learning to ignore. This includes taking a sales call for a new lead, running a short customer workshop, building customer use cases, writing internal documentation, building internal agents, and further building out our own AI support tooling. As our inference and cloud offering grows, you will increasingly help customers understand and adopt it. What You Will Do Front-line customer support. Millions look to us for unique activities they can trust, and it’s all powered by our commitment to make every single journey extraordinary - including yours. Ready to unlock your potential with a community of fellow explorers? Find your next role at our Berlin HQ or one of our local offices around the globe, from New York to Bangkok. Head to getyourguide.careers to take the first step. Team mission Internal Audit is a new function at GetYourGuide, built from the ground up to support the business through its next phase of growth and its journey toward the governance standards of a listed company. Our purpose is value preservation: helping protect what has been built as the company scales. We aim to be digitally native and AI-enabled - testing full populations with data rather than samples, and auditing how the company itself uses AI. As our first Senior Technology Audit Manager, you will own technology assurance across the company. You will deliver risk-based technology audits, lead Internal Audit's work over IT general controls and finance systems within the SOX programme, and build the continuous auditing capability that sits at the heart of how the function works. Your mission Building the function Shape our tech audit methodology and tooling, built on GetYourGuide’s own data and AI tools. Help run the annual risk assessment with engineering, security and data leaders. Explain technical observations in plain language to executives and the Audit Committee. Embed data analytics and AI into day-to-day audit work, turning audit objectives into analytical procedures that deliver evidence-based results. Technology audits Own technology audits end to end, across AI governance, marketplace integrity, change management, access, cloud, data and cyber. Test whether technology controls are well designed and work in practice, and turn observations into practical fixes. Co-ordinate with co-source specialists where deeper expertise is needed, while owning every conclusion. SOX: IT controls and finance systems Lead independent assurance over IT general controls across the systems behind financial reporting. Assess application controls, key reports and SOC 1 / SOC 2 reliance. Partner with Security, Tech Infrastructure, Engineering, Data Platform, Finance Systems, Legal and Internal Controls, as well as our external auditor and Internal Audit co-source partners. Drive tech deficiencies to validated closure and help prepare for external audit attestation. Continuous auditing Build and run our continuous auditing programme, testing full populations with rules, analytics, statistical models and AI agents. Extract and analyse data from finance and operational systems (e.g. SAP, Databricks) to surface anomalies, trends and control issues, and drive automation where relevant. Make every routine reliable, with validated data, documented logic and evidence that stands up to external audit. Hand proven routines to the business as their own controls, keeping the right to re-test. Turn data into clear stories and dashboards for process owners, management and the Audit Committee. Change and emerging risk Get involved early in major tech change, from system launches to automation and AI rollouts. Join incident reviews and respond quickly to emerging technology risks. Advise on cyber, data privacy and AI regulation as our controls mature. Your toolkit 8-10 years in IT audit, technology risk or technology assurance, ideally combining Big 4 (or similar) and in-house experience. A degree or background in data science, statistics, computer science or a related field is a strong plus. Deep, hands-on SOX experience over IT general controls and IT-dependent controls (scoping, testing, deficiency evaluation, IPE and SOC report reliance), plus familiarity with PCAOB expectations. jobs.title: Senior Data Engineer
jobs.description: About Abound We’re redefining consumer lending in the UK, and beyond. Using advanced AI and Open Banking data, we make fair, affordable personal finance available to more people. While traditional lenders rely almost entirely on credit scores, we look at the full financial picture - how much you spend, and what you can afford to repay to build a deeper, more accurate understanding of each customer's unique financial situation. And we've shown it works at scale. We’ve issued over £1.3bn in loans directly to customers while delivering market-leading credit performance - for every 10 defaults the industry expects, we see only 3. We also reached profitability just 2.5 years after launch. Backed by £2bn+ of funding from top-tier investors including Citi, GSR Ventures, and Deutsche Bank, we’re recognised as one of Europe’s fastest-growing fintechs (Sifted, CNBC). Now, we’re expanding into new markets and product lines - and we’re looking for ambitious people who want to learn fast, take ownership, and grow with us. About the role Abound is changing the face of lending. Our data lake will change the pace and the way we operate. It will power most of the decisions we make, from credit and pricing to operations and finance, and it is the foundation of our AI future. None of that works without data people can trust. Our data is our most valuable asset, and this role is its custodian. As our Senior Data Engineer, you will own the warehouse that turns raw data from underwriting, lending, open banking and finance into the facts the whole company runs on. You will help shape that future. Through a semantic layer and natural-language-to-SQL tools, anyone at Abound will be able to ask a question in plain English and get a correct answer in seconds. You decide how the model is built, what it measures, and how AI uses it. You will not start from a blank page. The first version of the warehouse is live, with real users and real problems to solve. This is an engineering role, not a SQL-only ETL job: you will write production Python and Spark, and work side by side with data science. Responsibilities Make the semantic layer and natural-language-to-SQL tools the way teams answer everyday questions. Define each metric with its business owner, and test that the tools return the agreed number. Own the warehouse design and modelling standards, and approve every change to it. Work with data scientists to turn their use cases into tested facts, dimensions and marts. Move features from the application backend, and reports from QuickSight, onto the lake, and prove they match the originals. Run and tune the Spark pipeline that feeds the warehouse, and fix performance bottlenecks in Spark and Athena. Own data quality, reconciliation and PII handling, and keep Glue and Athena costs in check. Mentor the engineers and analysts who contribute to the warehouse. What we're looking for You have owned a production warehouse before, and you can point to a dimensional model you designed and the decisions behind it. You write Python and Spark as confidently as SQL. 5+ years in data engineering, with at least 2 owning the design of a production warehouse or lakehouse. Proven dimensional modelling: conformed dimensions, fact grain, SCD2, and late-arriving or restated data. You can explain the trade-offs you made. Experience making data usable by AI: a semantic layer such as MetricFlow, Cube or LookML, natural-language-to-SQL or LLM agents over governed data, and checking that their answers are right. Strong dbt in production: incremental models, macros, tests and CI. Strong PySpark and Python: tuning jobs with the Spark UI, and reimplementing application logic on Spark with tests that prove both agree. Advanced SQL on a distributed engine, ideally Athena or Trino. BI experience, ideally QuickSight, including moving report logic out of the BI tool and into the warehouse. A track record of working with data scientists or analysts, turning loosely stated questions into mode

jobs.title: SIP Expert
jobs.description: About ElevenLabs ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology. We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always. We have expanded from voice into three main platforms: ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale. ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages. ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models. Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you. How we work High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy. Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you. AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations. Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models. Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location. What we offer Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities. Learning & development : ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend. Social travel : We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose. Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún Co-working : If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend. About the role We are looking for a SIP Expert to own the telephony layer that connects ElevenAgents voice agents to the phone network. SIP traffic is moving from early adoption to large enterprise call volumes, so the hard problems are now reliability and latency at scale. Your general responsibilities will include: Owning SIP end to end, from design doc to implementation, testing and ongoing operation, for a product used by enterprises at scale. Making call flows such as warm transfers dependable, and simplifying how our call services communicate with each other. Diagnosing and fixing load-related failures such as resource exhaustion and dropped connections. Collaborating with support, infrastructure and other teams to turn customer needs into shipped features. Specific responsibilities might include: Making our SIP edge and routing layer production-ready for large enterprise traffic. Designing and shipping lightweight, lower-latency call-handling services. Supporting carrier and SIP trunk integrations for enterprise customers. You will join a small team of five, reporting directly to the team lead, with a high degree of ownership and very little bureaucracy. jobs.title: AI Modelling and Simulation Engineer
jobs.description: The Opportunity Lumai is moving from optical-compute research into production AI systems, and the architecture and compiler decisions that shape the product are being made now, ahead of the silicon that will confirm them. This hire builds the modelling capability those decisions rest on. The Role You will own the performance and power modelling framework that predicts how Lumai's photonic AI hardware performs against real inference workloads, giving the architecture and compiler teams one shared source of truth for latency, throughput and power across device configurations. You will model the compute engines, interconnect, memory and bridge interfaces; keep the model honest by characterising operator-level workloads against hardware, RTL or emulation results; and turn what the model says into decisions teams act on. What is genuinely hard about this is balancing speed, fidelity and usability. The model has to capture concurrency, event-driven behaviour and compute-block latency in enough detail to support real architecture decisions, and still compare configurations in minutes rather than overnight. The gap between what the model predicts and what the hardware does has to be measured rather than assumed, and closing it is the part that never stops. What You'll Do Design, build and maintain a Python-based framework that models hardware and software latency, hardware concurrency and event-driven relationships. Model compute engines, interconnect and synchronisation fabric, memory and bridge interfaces, and accelerator blocks across device configurations. Characterise convolution, depthwise convolution, pooling, attention and other operator workloads against hardware, RTL or emulation results. Build compiler-agnostic interfaces that ingest compiled models and MLIR from multiple internal compiler flows. Analyse simulation traces with the architecture and compiler teams to improve layer-to-hardware mappings and resolve performance discrepancies. Run industry benchmarks and representative models - UL Procyon, Geekbench AI, Stable Diffusion and contemporary LLMs - to produce decision-ready KPIs. Develop block-level power models and validate worst-case power scenarios with the micro-architecture, verification and physical-design teams. Own the CI/CD pipelines and simulation flows that keep results reliable and reproducible as usage scales. Translate modelling findings into architecture and compiler decisions, setting technical direction and developing engineers or interns as the team grows. What We're Looking For Must-have Proven experience building or substantially extending a hardware/software performance modelling or simulation framework for AI/ML accelerators, ideally in Python. Strong understanding of hardware concurrency, event-driven modelling and AI inference accelerator micro-architecture: compute, memory hierarchy, interconnect and dataflow. jobs.title: Staff Infrastructure Engineer
jobs.description: About Antithesis We take cutting edge software-testing technologies and make them useful for finding real bugs in our customer’s software, allowing them to make more reliable software and ship with confidence. Historically we’ve focused on the hardest testing problems, providing deterministic simulation testing of whole distributed systems, finding and helping people to understand bugs that would have been a nightmare to find in production. As more and more code is written by agents, everyone is starting to realise just how important software verification is, and we’re in the process of expanding the problems and companies we target, and are providing an increasingly broad suite of open source and commercial testing tools for a much wider variety of problems and audiences. We’re well funded, deeply technical, and committed to improving the quality of software across the board. If you’d like to help us do that, we’d love to hear from you. About the Role You'd be joining a small London-based team building out a new Antithesis product, focusing on a more downmarket and diverse set of customers than our main product. We’re rapidly iterating and expect to be shipping some time early in the new year. We're looking for an engineer at the Senior to Staff level to help us make that system dependable. This will be “devops” in the traditional sense, though more dev than ops: You'll be a member of the engineering team, not a separate operations function, working in the same repository as everyone else, but your primary area of responsibility will be how the system runs in production. That means AWS, deployment, observability, alerting, and the on-call that comes with them. There will be some on-call, shared with the rest of the team, and part of the job will be helping us define how that works. This is the first product Antithesis is shipping primarily out of the UK, and we want to get things right from the start to make it sustainable and quiet. We’re thinking of this role as less about being the person that gets paged, and more being the person who tries to make sure that nobody does. Likely much of this will have already been prototyped by the time you join, but there will be a lot of latitude to make big changes to how that works. What You'll Do Own our AWS environment. Define and build out our observability and alerting Ensure our continuous deployment story is robust and stress-free in an environment where we expect to change production many times a day. Build and maintain our infrastructure for our fleet of testing VMs for running customers’ code. Take charge of our incident response and make sure we learn from incidents so we don’t repeat them. What We're Looking For An ideal candidate would have most of the following: You have been responsible for a production system on AWS, including being on call for it, and you have opinions about what you would do differently. Fluency with infrastructure as code and CI/CD. Practical experience of observability. You have built alerting that people trusted. Experience operating Postgres: backups, upgrades, migrations, and what happens when they go wrong. Solid Linux, container and networking fundamentals. You are comfortable directing AI coding agents and skeptical of what they produce. Bonus: Experience running agentic systems in production. Sandboxing or isolating untrusted code (microVMs, gVisor, or similar), or security work on a multi-tenant platform. Being the first infrastructure engineer on a team, or building an on-call rotation from nothing. Cost management for bursty, compute-heavy workloads. Nix. About Our Team Our team spans CS degrees, philosophy, mathematics, everything in between, or nothing formal at all. What everyone shares is a high bar for engineering quality. We work primarily in-person because it's how we build trust and tackle hard problems together. Location: This position is onsite, based in our London, UK office. We believe the future of medicine lies in reprogramming the body to repair itself, and we design the models and the medicines to teach it how. Our EDEN models are trained on BaseData, the world's largest proprietary genomic dataset, with over 10B genes collected through partnerships in more than 30 countries across all seven continents. This gives our AI models access to genetic diversity that doesn't exist in public databases, and enables EDEN to design cell and gene therapies, enzymes, and peptides directly from information about a disease. Our pipeline of EDEN-designed therapeutics, beginning with in vivo cell therapy, is advancing towards clinical development. In September 2026 we closed an oversubscribed $140M Series C led by S32, with participation from NVIDIA, Anthropic's Anthology Fund, Catalio, European Tech Collective, Firebrand River Capital, King Philanthropies, NATO Innovation Fund, NVentures (NVIDIA's venture arm), Redalpine, Rockefeller Foundation, Singular, Sovereign AI and True Ventures. At Basecamp Research, we pride ourselves on being a lean collaborative and global team with extremely specialist and unique skills. Our biologists, engineers, ML scientists and field explorers are united by a sense of adventure and the belief that AI, biology and data, will result in new medicines for patients who have few options today. The Role & Key Responsibilities The hands of the Trillion Gene Atlas. Operate and maintain laboratory automation. Work with automated liquid handling systems (including Myra9) and other platforms to process samples at batch scale. Perform routine maintenance, troubleshoot instrument issues, and flag deviations from expected performance. Maintain accurate records in LIMS. Log all sample processing steps, QC data, and observations in Benchling LIMS in real time. Ensure full traceability of every sample from receipt through to sequencing dispatch. Perform QC checks and flag anomalies. Carry out quantification, quality checks, and standard analytical assays at key pipeline stages. Identify out-of-specification results, escalate appropriately, and contribute to root cause investigations. Support R&D protocol testing. Maintain a safe, organised lab environment. Uphold high standards of lab hygiene, reagent management, and safety compliance including CL2 working practices. Help keep the lab stocked, organised, and ready to run at scale. Required Skills and Experience Hands-on laboratory experience in a molecular biology or life sciences setting - academic, commercial, or both Practical experience with DNA extraction from biological or environmental samples using kit-based and automated methods Comfortable working at high throughput with strong attention to detail - precise pipetting, consistent technique, reliable record-keeping Experience using LIMS or equivalent electronic lab notebook for sample tracking and data recording Ability to follow SOPs accurately, identify deviations, and escalate clearly and prompt

jobs.title: Alternant·e Growth Marketing Manager | Thiga Academy
jobs.description: Alternance · Paris 9e · Télétravail · rythme d’alternance souhaité 3 semaines entreprise / 1 semaine école    Thiga en 30 secondes :  Thiga est un cabinet de conseil spécialisé en IA et en digital. Nous accompagnons les plus grands groupes et scale-ups françaises : Decathlon, Doctolib, AXA, ManoMano, Mirakl, Disney, Leboncoin et une centaine d'autres. Nous sommes 200, majoritairement à Paris. Thiga Academy, c'est notre organisme de formation. On y forme les équipes produit (Product Managers, Product Owners, Designers, Product Leaders) et celles qui veulent le devenir : product management, product discovery, leadership produit, et IA appliquée au produit. En inter-entreprise comme en intra, on transmet ce que nos consultants pratiquent chez nos clients tous les jours   Pourquoi ce poste :  L'Academy forme chaque année 2000 professionnels et son offre est solide. Le problème : aujourd'hui, elle ne communique presque pas. Peu de contenu, peu de présence, une notoriété très en dessous de ce que le catalogue mérite. C'est une page blanche côté growth, et c'est exactement ce qui rend le poste intéressant. On cherche quelqu'un pour construire, mesurer et faire tourner le moteur d'acquisition de l'Academy à partir de zéro : quels canaux, quels messages, quel funnel, avec quels résultats. Pas pour décorer le catalogue, pour le remplir. Ce que tu vas faire 🖇 1. Construire et faire tourner le moteur d'acquisition, avec le Head of Marketing & Events Structurer le tunnel d'acquisition de bout en bout : quels canaux amènent du trafic, ce qui convertit en lead, ce qui déclenche l'inscription Tester des canaux et des formats en continu (LinkedIn organique et payant, email, SEO, partenariats, salons) et couper vite ce qui ne marche pas Créer et itérer les landing pages du catalogue et des sessions, pensées pour convertir dès le premier jet et retravaillées à partir de la donnée Mettre en place les séquences email dans HubSpot : nurturing, relances, réactivation des contacts dormants, avec un test A/B sur les objets et les CTA Accompagner le lancement des nouvelles formations avec un plan d'acquisition dédié, pas seulement un plan de com Créer les supports nécessaires au tunnel avec Figma (catalogue, plaquettes, brochures) en gardant en tête qu'un support existe pour convertir, pas pour exister Représenter l'Academy sur des salons et événements, avec un objectif de leads qualifiés en sortie, pas juste de présence 2. Mesurer, analyser, arbitrer Le nerf du poste. Sans mesure, pas de growth, juste du marketing qui se raconte des histoires. Suivre les KPIs qui comptent à chaque étape du tunnel : trafic, taux de clic, taux de conversion en lead, taux de conversion en inscrit, coût d'acquisition par inscrit, taux de remplissage des sessions Construire les dashboards HubSpot qui donnent une vision claire de ce qui marche, canal par canal, campagne par campagne Identifier où le tunnel fuit et proposer les hypothèses à tester pour colmater Faire remonter les résultats au Head of Marketing & Events pour arbitrer les prochains messages, offres et canaux, avec des chiffres, pas des impressions 3. Faire vivre la marque et la communauté qui nourrissent le funnel L'acquisition ne marche pas sans contenu ni preuve sociale. C'est le carburant du tunnel. Poser la ligne éditoriale et la faire vivre : posts LinkedIn, articles, newsletters, formats courts autour du product et de l'IA Animer la relation avec les alumni et la communauté d'apprenants : témoignages, cas concrets, un bouche-à-oreille qu'on peut transformer en canal d'acquisition mesurable L'IA n'est pas une option chez nous , c'est la pierre angulaire de notre façon de travailler, et on attend de toi que tu aies cette fibre. Concrètement, tu t'appuieras sur l'IA à chaque étape : générer et itérer des variantes de copies avec Claude, produire des visuels avec Nano Banana et Figma, des teasers avec HeyGen, ou transformer une transcription Granola en article et en carrousel

jobs.title: Financial Crime Lead
jobs.description: What is Finary? Money is broken: most people’s wealth sits in products they did not choose, with fees they cannot see. We are putting a private banker in everyone’s pocket, with the same quality of advice for a €10K saver and a €10M client. Mounir launched Finary in 2021, and more than 1M people now track their wealth with us. Finary AI turns that context into a plan, and our investment products and in-house wealth advisors (Finary One) make it real. Why now? AI makes this possible, and 3 things make it hard to copy: years of per-user financial data that no public dataset holds, a brand that brings in half of our new users through our own channels, and licences (PSAN, Investment Firm, MiCA) we secured before they became mandatory. We raised €40M from Hedosophia, Y Combinator and Speedinvest. Founders and leaders from Qonto, Photoroom, Bitpanda, UBS and Wise also invested. What we offer We’re 70 builders with real ownership from day 1, tier-1 salary and equity, and offices in central Paris with hybrid remote. Our culture is direct and built on radical candor. AI is a real bar here: everyone has rebuilt how they work around it. Read more about our values here . The opportunity More than 1M people track and grow their wealth with Finary. In 2021, when a simple registration was enough to offer crypto in France, we chose to build fully regulated. Today Finary is a crypto-asset service provider under MiCA, an investment firm, a payment institution and an insurance broker. Very few European platforms hold that combination. Our compliance team is organised by role, not by product: compliance officer, AML, senior advisory and control. Each role covers every licence. Reporting to our Head of Compliance, who is our AML/CFT officer, you'll work alongside our AML analyst and take ownership of the framework that protects our clients and our licences, with most of our exposure in crypto. What you'll do Lead the AML/CFT framework: procedures, client risk classification, detection rules and tools (screening, blockchain analytics, Travel Rule), calibrated on our own data. Investigate and decide the hard cases: enhanced reviews of individuals and companies (ownership chains, financial statements, flows), on-chain investigations, decisions on suspicion. Draft and file suspicious transaction reports, and act as deputy TRACFIN declarant and correspondent. Handle screening and asset freezing: PEP, sanctions and adverse media hits, list updates. Build with AI: design and tune the agents and rules in our back-office tool that prepare files and clear first-level reviews, and keep the decision on suspicion human. Work with Ops, Care, Product and our outsourced review team so that AML decisions are clear, fast and fair to the honest majority of our clients. What we're looking for You've spent 6 to 8 years in AML/CFT in financial services, including hands-on work at a crypto-asset service provider (PSAN/CASP). You've drafted and filed suspicious transaction reports with TRACFIN yourself. You investigate on-chain: you use blockchain analytics tools and you know the Travel Rule and self-hosted wallets. You hold a certification in on-chain analysis (Chainalysis CCI, CCCA or CRC, or a TRM Labs or Elliptic equivalent) and a Travel Rule certification (Notabene NB-TRFC or equivalent). You work with data and AI every day: you query data yourself and you already use AI in your reviews or investigations. This is a must, not a plus. You decide on evidence, you keep weak signals in proportion, and you explain your decisions clearly. You prioritise a growing queue by risk without missing a legal deadline, and you move the framework forward at the same time. Fluent French and professional English. This role is not for you if you'd rather stay on onboarding checks, you prefer advising to deciding, or you need a large financial crime department and mature tools before you can start. You don't tick every box? Apply anyway if you've done the core of the job: investigating

jobs.title: Product Designer - Paris
jobs.description: As a Product Designer, you'll work on the H Platform, where our users create and run agentic AI workflows powered by our models. Nobody has written the playbook for designing these experiences yet. Our next stage is making the platform truly useful for its users and levelling it up, in design as much as in technology, and you'll build the product experiences that deliver real value in organisations. At H Company, we believe AI should take action in the real world, and our mission is to make agentic AI genuinely useful for large organisations. We're pioneers in computer use: our own vision-language models power agents that see, click and type their way through the software businesses already run, with no integrations or rebuilds, and we own the whole stack, from research and models to the products built on top of them. What you'll be doing Talking to our users constantly to understand their needs and figure out what will make the platform truly useful for them. Turning those insights into research and explorations, looking at problems from different angles before settling on a direction. Picking the right tool for each task: a Figma design, a prototype, or a small PR when a quick change is the fastest way to ship. Testing what you build with users, measuring its impact (A/B testing, user interviews, users daily use data...) and iterating quickly based on what you learn. Shaping the roadmap together with the whole team, engineers and PMs alike. Who you'll work with The role sits in our Product team, which is responsible for product direction, strategy and design. You'll join the product designer who owns design and UX today, and work closely with product, engineering and forward deployed engineers. What we think it takes Above all, we want someone who cares deeply about users, has great product taste and can explain it, moves fast while keeping quality high, leaves their ego at the door and welcomes feedback. Likely a good fit if you Have 5+ years of experience as a Product Designer at tech companies. Have excellent UX, UI and interaction design skills, and can make complex, technical flows, like building and running AI agent workflows, feel simple and intuitive. Have a portfolio that shows your latest work. Have hands-on experience running user tests and A/B tests. Know when a proven solution is good enough and when a problem deserves something new. Have designed complex data or ML/AI-driven products: you know how to make complex systems understandable and how to design for AI behaviour that isn't always predictable, building trust and keeping users in control. Are comfortable in technical discussions: you can dig into constraints and trade-offs with engineers and ramp up quickly on technical topics to discuss them with our researchers and more technical engineers. Are fluent in Figma. Can work within a design system and contribute to it. Stronger still if you Have designed platforms: complex B2B web or desktop software used by professionals, whether that's tools to build and run workflows, big data and analytics software, operational dashboards or other data-dense interfaces. Are curious about code and AI in your design workflow. Every design team is still figuring out how AI changes the way we work, and we're no different, so we'd love someone who has started experimenting, whether by prototyping in code, building small tools or bringing AI into their process, and who wants to keep exploring with us. If you match most of this but not every point, apply anyway. We care far more about how you think, your curiosity and your care for users than a perfect match. How we hire Four stages: a 30-minute call with our Talent team, a 60-minute portfolio review, a 60-minute design interview in person at our Paris office, and a closing 30-minute conversation. The portfolio review and design interview are built around your own work and how you design. Please apply with your CV and a link to your portfolio showing your latest work. Find Jobs

You will embed with enterprise clients to take AI-powered products from discovery to pilot, production and adoption, using PALO IT's AI-first Gen-e²™ methodology. A client-facing consulting posture and 5+ years of hands-on engineering are required. Who We Are Building the AI-first frontier enterprise. We are a global technology consultancy with a trademarked, AI-first approach—Gen-e2™. It redefines how enterprises build digital products and transform their organizations with AI. We do the right thing, and we do it right. We're proud to be a World Economic Forum New Champion, and a B Corp-certified company. · We are small enough to care locally, big enough to deliver globally (10 countries, 450+ experts from 50+ nationalities) · We are becoming an agentic organization , adopting the AI-native operating model we bring to our clients. · We are robust and resilient (100% independent, 0 debt, founded 2009) · We are AI-native professionals who invest in what we believe and work as a collective intelligence · We are positive, courageous and deliver at the leading edge What does a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer do at PALO IT? As a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer at PALO IT in Paris, you embed with client engineering, product and domain teams at large enterprises, and own the journey from discovery and scoping to pilot, production and adoption. Think deploying an agentic AI workflow inside a health insurer, standing up an AI-powered platform for a bank, or designing intelligent automation for an energy leader. This is not staff augmentation: you build like a product engineer and own whether what you ship gets adopted and creates value. Client delivery · Deliver defined workstreams independently, from prototype through to production · Frame ambiguous business problems in discovery and scoping sessions, asking the clarifying questions that shape the solution · Build full-stack, AI-powered systems that deliver measurable client impact · Surface risks and dependencies before they become blockers, and pick up unassigned work to drive it forward Consulting & client engagement · Build trust with technical and non-technical stakeholders, and present your thinking to senior decision-makers · Propose how AI can improve the client's product beyond what was asked · Bring field feedback back to the team to sharpen how PALO IT delivers AI-native practice with Gen-e²™ · Work AI-first by default: GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor or Codex generate most of your requirements, code and architecture diagrams · Apply prompt and context engineering, and critically review every AI-generated output, AI generates; engineers own · Scout emerging GenAI tools and turn them into practical improvements for the team What makes this role different at PALO IT? With Gen-e²™, PALO IT generates 95% of a product, code, documentation, infrastructure as code and design with AI coding agents and its own tooling, and delivers end-to-end products 2–3× faster than traditional approaches. You will work hands-on with the latest AI tooling from Microsoft, GitHub, Anthropic and other global technology leaders, and help define what AI-native delivery looks like inside the enterprises PALO IT transforms. If ambiguity energises you more than a well-defined backlog, you'll thrive here. What experience do you need for this role? Must-haves · A client-facing, consulting posture, non-negotiable. jobs.title: Senior Full Stack Engineer - AdManager
jobs.description: Streaming TV is no longer just a brand awareness channel. It’s becoming a core part of the performance marketing mix, alongside search and social. Vibe.co is building the platform that makes TV work like the rest of the acquisition stack: targeted, measurable, and optimized for results. Vibe.co is an Audience First Streaming TV Advertising platform that gives marketers the tools to reach the right audiences, optimize campaigns in real time, and understand what’s actually driving business outcomes. With hyper-targeted segmentation, AI-powered recommendations, real-time optimization, and incrementality measurement, Vibe brings the precision and accountability of digital advertising to the biggest screen in the house. Today, more than 12,000 brands use Vibe.co to reach 120 million+ households. And in August 2026, Vibe.co became a Walmart company, opening up a new chapter for the business and the industry. With Walmart’s first-party data and purchase signals now part of the Vibe platform, advertisers can connect TV advertising to real-world transactions and measure the impact of CTV with a level of precision previously associated with platforms like Google and Meta. This is a unique moment to join Vibe. With Walmart’s scale, data, and reach behind us, we’re building the next generation of TV advertising and creating a more measurable, performance-driven future for the channel. About the Role You’ll join AdManager, the team behind everything advertisers touch in Vibe: campaign setup, performance reporting, creatives management, integrations, payments, and account management. jobs.title: Ingénieur ou post-doctorant pour l'analyse des données acquises par un radar HF océanographique couvrant le Raz Blanchard
jobs.company: ECOLE NATIONALE SUPERIEURE DE TECHNIQUES AVANCEES
jobs.description: ENSTA, établissement d’enseignement supérieur et de recherche sous tutelle du ministère des Armées, développe des activités de formation, de recherche et d’innovation dans les domaines de la défense et de la sécurité, des transports, de l'énergie, des activités maritimes, du numérique et de la santé. L’école, présente sur deux campus, à Paris-Saclay et à Brest, est membre de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris. Classée dans le Top 10 des meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France, elle a pour mission : la formation d’élèves ingénieurs civils et militaires, de cadres et docteurs pour les secteurs public et privé, la recherche et l’innovation de haut niveau en relation étroite avec l’industrie des grands secteurs de souveraineté au sein de 6 unités de formation et de recherche (UFR). Le/la titulaire du poste sera affecté au sein de l’UFR S2I sur le Campus de Brest.   Projet FLOWATT Le projet FLOWATT, dans le cadre duquel s’inscrit cette étude, vise à déployer et exploiter six hydroliennes dans les forts courants marins du Raz Blanchard, en Normandie. Au-delà de la production d’énergie, FLOWATT a pour objectif d’évaluer le potentiel du Raz Blanchard pour le déploiement de fermes hydroliennes à plus grande échelle. Cette évaluation repose notamment sur une caractérisation précise de la ressource, une estimation fine du productible et une meilleure compréhension des impacts environnementaux. Pour répondre à ces enjeux, le projet combine mesures in situ, modélisation numérique et essais expérimentaux afin de fournir les connaissances nécessaires à la préparation des futurs déploiements commerciaux, tout en contribuant à la réduction des coûts de production et à la limitation des impacts sur l’environnement marin. Dans ce contexte, la caractérisation de l’état de mer constitue un enjeu important, notamment dans une zone soumise à des courants très intenses. La présente étude s’intéresse ainsi aux données de radar HF acquises depuis fin 2017, ainsi qu’à celles qui seront nouvellement enregistrées dans le cadre du projet TidalRace. Le système, de technologie WERA, est réparti sur deux sites distants d’environ 5 km au Cap de la Hague et fonctionne à deux fréquences, 13,5 MHz et 24,5 MHz. Les acquisitions sont réalisées en continu, à raison de quatre mesures par heure, 24 h/24 et 7 j/7, sur une emprise couvrant l’ensemble du Raz Blanchard. Cette couverture temporelle et spatiale offre ainsi une opportunité unique de suivre l’évolution des états de mer dans des conditions hydrodynamiques particulièrement contraintes. L’exploitation de ces données nécessite toutefois d’adapter les méthodes de traitement aux conditions de forts courants. L’objectif des travaux est donc d’améliorer les algorithmes existants et, si nécessaire, d’en développer de nouveaux afin de restituer de manière fiable les spectres d’énergie des vagues en fréquence et en direction, ainsi que les paramètres moyens associés. Une première étape consistera à comprendre les limites des méthodes actuelles, qui ne permettent plus de restituer un état de mer cohérent avec les références disponibles lorsque la vitesse du courant dépasse 1 m/s, comme montré par Lopez et al. (2018). Les méthodes développées seront ensuite évaluées à partir des mesures in situ et des modélisations numériques. Le radar HF constitue ainsi un élément central de ce travail, dont l’amélioration doit permettre de mieux caractériser les états de mer dans les forts courants du Raz Blanchard . Missions / Activités principales : Le (la) titulaire du poste sera affecté à l’équipe M3 de l’UMR Lab-STICC et sera en charge des missions principales suivantes : Réaliser une étude bibliographique sur les modèles permettant de décrire l’effet des vagues sur le spectre Doppler mesuré par un radar HF Implémenter un code de simulation intégrant l’effet des vagues à partir d’une description de l’état de mer dans le spectre Doppler Analyser les simulations en les comparant aux mesures réelles pour comprendre l’in

Every new site tests how a robot understands its surroundings and chooses where to go: a ramp the planner avoids, a narrow passage that exposes a poor route, a gate that changes the map, a person who steps into the robot's path, or localization drift that builds over a long patrol. You treat those cases as the real navigation problem to solve, not as edge cases. You'll shape the technical choices behind reliable navigation, from sensor selection, ground segmentation, and traversability estimation to predicting how people and vehicles move and planning safe, efficient routes around them. Behavior prediction: anticipate how people, vehicles, and other dynamic obstacles will move, and plan routes that stay safe and efficient around them. New autonomy capabilities: work with the engineers building the operator application and backend so operator requests and new robot capabilities rest on a sound navigation design. The field feedback loop: work closely with forward-deployed engineers to turn site issues into bugs, design changes, and improvements to the navigation stack. Regular site visits to build a practical understanding of how robots and sensors behave in real operating conditions. About the Role As an FPGA Engineer Intern on Harmattan AI’s compute module team, you will take camera aggregation from concept to real hardware for the first time. Responsibilities Integrate existing IP cores, write HDL wrappers, simulate and validate FPGA logic that merges multiple camera streams into one. Investigate the system’s limits in camera count, resolution and frame rate. Build the processor-side pipeline that splits the merged stream so each camera stays independently usable. Debug the full chain, from cables and connectors to FPGA logic and camera software on the processor. Deliver a complete demonstrator and documentation that guide our next hardware design. Previous hands-on experience with FPGAs and digital board design and debugging. Experience writing software that runs close to the hardware; embedded Linux is a plus. Ideally, previous exposure to video or camera interfaces. Hands-on in the lab and comfortable reworking wiring, connectors and test setups to get a system running. jobs.description: About Us Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces. Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected. About the role As the composite technician on the Airframe team, your core mission is to prototype carbon structures fast, in-house — from mould to finished, quality-checked part — and to bring innovative solutions that make assembly and prototyping easier . A true hands-on professional, you combine technical skills, initiative, and a maker mindset. You build tooling, lay up and finish composite parts (carbon / glass fibre), and turn the engineers' CAD into flight-worthy structures on short cycles. You are also the owner of technical drawings and supplier quotations for the parts you handle, and the one who trains production operators when a design moves to series. You thrive with minimal supervision, favour pragmatic, quick-result approaches over perfect-but-slow tooling, and are equally comfortable laying up a part, machining or printing a mould, and reading a technical drawing. Technical skills Key responsibilities Rapid in-house prototyping (core) Produce carbon prototype structures quickly in-house, choosing the fastest viable route rather than heavy tooling when a proto is the goal. Propose innovative, simple solutions to speed up assembly and prototyping. Design certain parts and prototyping tools yourself (fixtures, adapters, simple structural parts) when it is faster than going through the design loop. Iterate fast with the design engineers: short loops between concept, part and feedback, flagging manufacturability issues before they cost a mould. Tooling & moulds Build and maintain moulds and tooling, in coordination with the design team; machine or 3D-print mould masters, prepare and polish mould surfaces. Design and build layup jigs, trimming templates, bonding and assembly fixtures. Manage the composite workshop consumables and material inventory (fabrics, resins, cores, vacuum consumables) including storage and shelf-life follow-up. Design & documentation Read and interpret 2D/3D drawings and ply books; model simple parts and tooling in CAD when needed; give manufacturability feedback early. Own the technical drawings: produce and keep up to date the manufacturing drawings for the parts and tooling you handle. Write and maintain clear, accessible fabrication procedures, ply books and cure logs on Confluence so processes are repeatable by others. Optimise part designs for their manufacturing process: adapt geometries for plastic injection (wall thickness, draft angles, ribs) or for composite / 3D-printed fabrication (layup feasibility, demoulding, printability), in collaboration with the design engineers. Support & improvement Support assembly and mechanical testing, including preparing test coupons and samples for structural analysis. Identify and propose process and quality improvements; help run the composite workshop safely (dust extraction, PPE, resin handling and waste management). Own the knowledge transfer to production: train the production operators on fabrication and assembly processes, and validate that a process is repeatable by others before handover. Candidate profile Technical diploma or degree in composite materials, mechanical / aerospace manufacturing, industrial technology, or equivalent hands-on experience. Proven experience in rapid in-house composite prototyping (carbon / glass fibre): hand layup, vacuum bagging, infusion and/or prepreg; mould making and surface preparation a strong plus. Track record of quick, pragmatic

jobs.title: Engineering Manager, Customs
jobs.description: <div class="content-intro"><h2><strong>About Flexport:&nbsp;</strong></h2> <p>At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.&nbsp;</p> <p>The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.</p></div><h3><strong>Why Customs Matters More Than Ever</strong></h3> <p>International trade is under more pressure than ever before. With tariffs, shifting regulations, and geopolitical uncertainty, customs has gone from a back-office function to a boardroom priority. The recent trade crisis — sparked by Trump-era tariffs — has made customs the single most complex challenge for global businesses. For many, it’s the difference between keeping supply chains moving or grinding them to a halt.</p> <p>That’s where we come in. The <strong>Customs Technology team</strong> at Flexport is leading the charge. We are building the systems that help entrepreneurs and global brands navigate complexity, stay compliant, and keep the world’s goods flowing.</p> <h3><strong>The Opportunity</strong></h3> <p>Customs brokerage is one of the largest, most under-innovated opportunities in logistics. Legacy customs brokers are stuck with outdated systems and manual processes—they simply can’t adapt fast enough.</p> <p>Flexport is growing fast because we’re different. jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.description: The challenge An entrepreneur chasing an unpaid invoice in Lagos. A shop owner confirming a shipment in Guangzhou. A consultant navigating a bank's phone menu in London. Today we serve them with a consumer app. Tomorrow we want to be the obvious way small businesses call the world. We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to own and scale the Calling for Work product proposition from 1 to 100. There's no mature roadmap to inherit: you'll write it, test it with customers and scale what works, with our Product & Tech team, to deliver a step change in segment growth. Shape the business proposition: Define what Talk360's business offer is and how it's priced, together with our commercial teams. Learn from customers continuously: Use interviews, surveys, support tickets and app store reviews to turn pains into a ranked opportunity roadmap. Experiment fast: Ship small bets, A/B test the journeys that matter, observe real world behaviour and turn results into roadmap decisions. Lead delivery: Work in an agile Product & Tech team; keep scope tight, priorities clear and releases flowing. AI-native execution: Use AI across discovery, specs, analysis and prototyping, and help shape how the team builds with AI. Partner across the business: Work with Revenue, Marketing, Support and Data on go-to-market, acquisition, retention and the metrics that show we're winning. The Team You'll join a lean Product & Engineering team where product, design, mobile, web, backend, VoIP and QA work closely together. No silos, no layers: turn a customer insight on Monday into a live experiment by Friday. What you’ll bring 5+ years in product management, including owning a product line or new proposition end to end. A track record of scaling a product from early traction, with commercial results to show. Hands-on experience with B2B, SMB or prosumer products; telecoms is a plus. Strong discovery skills: customer interviews, research synthesis and jobs-to-be-done thinking. Experimentation fluency: A/B testing, product analytics (Mixpanel or similar) and data analysis and data-driven decision making. Experience optimising MAU, ARPU, LTV, retention and conversion, with the business acumen to make strategic and tactical calls. Experience leading agile, cross-functional mobile product teams, with the technical depth to discuss trade-offs with engineers. Active, daily use of AI across your product workflow: research, analysis, specs and prototyping. Who you are Growth mindset: You're energised by building a playbook that doesn't exist yet. Ambitious and pragmatic: You aim for 100 but ship the smallest thing that proves the next step. Owner: You act without waiting for permission and own outcomes, not output. Customer-obsessed: You'd rather talk to five customers than debate one assumption. Clear communicator: You align engineers, leadership and partners around one simple story. jobs.description: Amsterdam or Antwerp – As a Backend Engineer within the GenAI Platform team, you help build the foundation that enables AI products across DPG Media. You design and develop scalable backend solutions that support identity, access management and platform insights for a growing portfolio of AI services. Ready to make an impact on the future of AI at DPG Media? Read on! What will you do? As a Backend Engineer, you take ownership of the platform capabilities that enable teams across DPG Media to securely use and manage AI products. You build backend services that unify user, access, usage and cost data while making architectural decisions that support the platform's continued growth. Your work ensures that new products and teams can be onboarded efficiently and consistently. You do this by: li]:mb-1 [&>li::marker]:text-base [&>li::marker]:text-gray-900 dark:[&>li::marker]:text-gray-100"> Defining how users, roles and permissions are managed centrally and applied consistently across every product on the GenAI Platform. Building backend services that collect, combine and expose usage, cost and user data for the platform portal and reporting. Designing scalable platform architecture that continues to perform as the number of products grows. Defining how platform resources are described so new products and teams can be added through configuration instead of custom development. Who are we? We are a small team that builds and operates the GenAI Platform used across DPG Media. The platform runs on Kubernetes and provides teams throughout the organisation with access to AI products, ranging from workflow automation to model hosting. What makes you the ideal candidate? For this role, we are looking for an experienced backend engineer who combines strong technical expertise with ownership and a pragmatic mindset. You are proactive, analytical and enjoy building scalable platform solutions. In addition, you bring: li]:mb-1 [&>li::marker]:text-base [&>li::marker]:text-gray-900 dark:[&>li::marker]:text-gray-100"> Around 5 years of backend engineering experience, including designing systems yourself. Proficiency in at least one backend language. We work with Go, TypeScript and Python, and you are willing to work across these technologies. Experience integrating third-party APIs and combining data from multiple sources into one consistent view. Hands-on experience with OAuth2/OIDC, role-based access models and running services on Kubernetes. Experience adding metrics and alerts to the services you build. Additional experience with Go, Kubernetes controllers or operators, declarative reconcile-based systems, usage metering, FinOps data, Terraform or GenAI systems is considered an advantage. How do you work? You take ownership of your work from design through delivery and beyond. You focus on delivering practical solutions first and continuously improve them. You proactively identify opportunities for improvement, clearly explain your reasoning and remain open to alternative perspectives. You think ahead when making design decisions and build with long-term scalability in mind. Our stack li]:mb-1 [&>li::marker]:text-base [&>li::marker]:text-gray-900 dark:[&>li::marker]:text-gray-100"> Languages: Go for the platform control plane, TypeScript and Python for services and APIs. Platform: Kubernetes (EKS) on AWS, Terraform, Helm and ArgoCD. Observability: Grafana, Prometheus and OpenTelemetry. CI/CD: GitHub Actions. At DPG Media, we are open to all talent in society. Regardless of your background, we invite you to apply for this position. It is precisely through the differences between colleagues that surprising insights and innovative solutions emerge. jobs.description: UFORCE exists to make aggression unaffordable. Founded in Ukraine and headquartered in London, UFORCE is a defence-technology company with operations across Europe, the United States and Asia. UFORCE builds uncrewed vessels, ground robotics and aircraft, autonomy software, and the command-and-control layer that operates them together. Each platform is deployable on its own, and stronger as part of the system. Its product lines include the MAGURA family of uncrewed surface vessels, the NEMESIS family of strike platforms, the LIUT family of ground robotic platforms, and counter-UAS systems. About the role Uforce is scaling quickly, and our order book is beginning to outgrow site-by-site planning. We are hiring a Global Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) / Demand Planning Manager to own the link between what we expect to sell and what our production network can build. This is a global role by design: rather than sitting inside any one facility, you will hold the bird's-eye view across our entire network — our Portugal operations, our Poole location, and the US sites we are building out — so that demand is matched to capacity wherever it makes the most sense. What you'll do You will own the bookings forecast on a regular cadence (initially weekly), looking out over the next several months to a quarter. You'll translate that forecast into a granular view of expected units — by platform, by drone/vessel type, and down to the configuration level — and keep it current as deals progress, slip, or change scope. You'll work closely with Sales to pressure-test the pipeline and with Finance and leadership to make sure everyone is operating from one shared number. With that forecast in hand, you will map incoming demand against available capacity at each site and get ahead of it. For example, if the forecast shows an order for 12 boats landing in the next two months, you'll be the one flagging it early, determining where it should be built, and working with the Portugal team (or whichever site is best placed) to plan materials, labor, and schedule well before the PO arrives. You'll identify capacity gaps and bottlenecks across the network, recommend where to load or shift work between sites, and help inform where and when we need to add capacity as the US footprint grows. Over time, you'll build the S&OP process itself: the regular forecast and capacity review rhythm, the planning tools and dashboards that support it, and the metrics (forecast accuracy, capacity utilization, on-time delivery) that tell us whether it is working. What we're looking for We're looking for someone with experience in demand planning, S&OP, or production planning at a hardware or manufacturing company, ideally one that scaled quickly across multiple sites. You're comfortable moving between a sales pipeline and a factory floor schedule, you're strong with data and forecasting models, and you can turn an uncertain forecast into clear, early decisions that site teams can act on. You communicate well across functions and time zones, and you're energized by building a process from the ground up rather than inheriting one. Experience in high-growth environments (automotive, aerospace, defense, robotics, or similar) is a strong plus, as is comfort with travel between our sites. The nature of combat has changed.
